item.title: Litigation-Related Update: Sileiri Doe Class Members May Request Reopening or Reconsideration of an Adverse Decision Without a Fee
item.description: On Sept. 28, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts issued an order requiring DHS to remediate certain adverse consequences for the class of aliens paroled into the United States after scheduling an appointment through the CBP One mobile app, and whose parole was terminated by the federal government via mass email in April 2025. Sileiri Doe v. DHS, 1:25-cv-12245-ADB (D. Mass).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Aliens in Idaho Charged for Illegal Voting
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services assisted an investigation that resulted in charges against two Canadian aliens residing in eastern Idaho for unlawfully voting in the 2022 general election.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) is opening an asylum office in Charlotte, North Carolina.

item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services provided critical assistance to the investigation leading to the conviction of a former medical doctor for naturalization fraud.

item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services provided critical assistance in the investigation that led to a federal indictment charging [name withheld], 60, an Italian national, with voting by an alien, attempting to unlawfully procure naturalization, and making a false statement in connection with naturalization.

item.title: USCIS Announces FY 2027 Inflation Increase for Certain Immigration-Related Fees
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has issued a Federal Register notice that will increase certain H.R. 1 immigration-related fees for fiscal year 2027.

item.title: USCIS Adjusts EB-5 Fees to Cover Program Costs and Strengthen Integrity Measures
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) is updating fees for the EB-5 Immigrant Investor Program to ensure EB-5 fees fully recover the cost of operating the program, meet statutory processing time goals, and support integrity measures such as audits and site visits.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Assists Florida Investigation Leading to Charges for Unlawful Voting
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services provided critical assistance to investigations that resulted in charges against 16 aliens accused of unlawfully voting in Florida elections.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Cuban Alien Convicted for International Alien Smuggling and Money Laundering Conspiracy
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services played a critical role in the investigation that led to the conviction of [name withheld], 28, of Hialeah, Florida, for his role in an international alien smuggling and money laundering conspiracy.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Aliens Charged with Illegally Voting and Making False Statements While Applying for US Citizenship
item.description: An Essex County man and a Middlesex County woman, both aliens, were charged with illegally voting in a federal election and making false statements while applying for U.S. citizenship.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Nigerian Alien Indicted for Illegally Voting
item.description: A federal grand jury in Topeka returned an indictment charging a Nigerian alien with falsely claiming to be a U.S. citizen to illegally vote in elections.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Romanian Alien Admits Conspiring to Commit Marriage Fraud
item.description: A Romanian alien admitted to conspiring with an American citizen to enter into a sham marriage so that she could obtain U.S. citizenship. U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services assisted the investigation.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Haitian Alien Pleads Guilty to Illegally Voting in 2024 Election
item.description: A Haitian alien pleaded guilty Sept. 22 in federal court to falsely claiming U.S. citizenship to register to vote and casting a ballot in the 2024 general election.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Man Charged with Naturalization Fraud; Three Others Face Denaturalization
item.description: A federal grand jury in Charlotte returned a criminal indictment charging [name withheld], 42, a naturalized citizen from Bhutan, with naturalization fraud.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Chinese Aliens Indicted on Naturalization and Firearms Charges
item.description: Two Chinese aliens turned themselves in Sept. 17 on charges that accuse one of a naturalization crime and both of a firearm crime. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Missouri made the announcement.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Bosnian Prisoner Abuser Charged with Lying to Get US Citizenship
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services provided vital assistance to an investigation that lead to the indictment of [name withheld], an alien and accused war criminal from Bosnia and Herzegovina.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Five Defendants Charged with Defrauding and Exploiting H-2A Visa Program to Smuggle Aliens into the United States
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) supported a federal investigation that resulted in the indictment of five people for their roles in a scheme to exploit a nonimmigrant visa worker program. The defendants fraudulently obtained worker visas and smuggled aliens into the United States. The U.S. Attorney for Southern District of Georgia made the announcement.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Immigration Attorney Arrested in Alleged Fraud Scheme
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services provided pivotal assistance to an investigation leading to the indictment and arrest of a Houston area immigration attorney.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Peruvian Alien Indicted for Illegally Voting
item.description: A federal grand jury in Wichita indicted a Peruvian alien with multiple criminal offenses arising from allegedly voting in a federal election despite not being a U.S. citizen.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Department of Justice Removes Alien Terrorist in First Use of United States Alien Terrorist Removal Court
item.description: In the first-ever case before the United States Alien Terrorist Removal Court (ATRC), [name withheld], 47, an Afghan national previously residing in Fort Worth, Texas, was removed from the United States after conceding that she is an alien terrorist.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Reaches H-2B Cap for First Half of FY 2027
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services received enough petitions to meet the congressionally established H-2B cap for the first half of fiscal year (FY) 2027.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Announces Rule for Certain Children Born in the United States to Foreign Government Employees
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security today issued an interim final rule amending its regulations to allow certain children born in the United States to foreign government employees who are not U.S. citizens to register as lawful permanent residents.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Court Order on Diversity Immigrant Visa Program Hold Policy
item.description: On Aug. 28, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California issued an order in Medani, et al., v. Trump, et al., 26-cv-6332 (NDCA), temporarily vacating PM-602-0193 pending further litigation. USCIS is ordered, “to the extent practicable and in good faith, to take all reasonable steps during the remainder of the Diversity Visa fiscal year to resume ordinary adjudication of plaintiffs’ pending adjustment of status applications without applying” PM-602-0193.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Naturalized U.S. Citizen Indicted for Lying to Obtain U.S. Citizenship After Committing Felonies
item.description: A naturalized U.S. citizen made his initial appearance in court Sept. 2 for allegedly lying about his prior criminal acts to obtain U.S. citizenship. The U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Nevada announced the charges.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Opens New International Field Office in Ethiopia to Support Fraud Prevention
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) is opening a new international field office in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The office will begin operations on September 9, 2026, and will handle USCIS immigration matters in Ethiopia.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Illegal Alien Indicted in Marriage-Related Immigration Fraud
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services played a critical role in the investigation that led to the indictment of [name withheld], 38, a Peruvian alien illegally present in the United States, after federal prosecutors presented evidence to a grand jury.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Aunt and U.S. Airman Nephew Arrested in Immigration Fraud Scheme
item.description: Defendants allegedly lied about their relationship to obtain immigration benefits
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Recent Court Order on Hold Policies
item.description: On Aug. 24, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California issued an order in Red Eagle Law, L.C., et al., v. Joseph B. Edlow, 26-cv-04850-CRB (NDCA), enjoining PM 602-0192, and PM 602-0194.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Reaches Fiscal Year 2027 H-1B Cap
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has received enough petitions to reach the congressionally mandated 65,000 H-1B visa regular cap and the 20,000 H-1B visa U.S. advanced degree exemption, known as the master’s cap, for fiscal year 2027.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Terminates Temporary Protected Status for Yemen
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security has posted a Federal Register notice regarding the termination of Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Yemen.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Terminates Temporary Protected Status for Yemen
item.description: Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem today announced the termination of Temporary Protected Status for Yemen. The termination is effective 60 days after the notice is published in the Federal Register.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS to Increase Premium Processing Fees
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is publishing a final rule that will increase USCIS fees for premium processing to reflect the amount of inflation from June 2023 through June 2025.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Ends Automatic Extension of Employment Authorization
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security has announced an interim final rule ending the practice of automatically extending employment authorization documents for aliens filing renewal applications in certain employment authorization categories.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Presidential Proclamation on Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers
item.description: On September 19, 2025, the President issued a Proclamation, Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers, an important initial step to reform the H-1B nonimmigrant visa program.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Implements New Immigration Parole Fee Required by H.R. 1
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security is publishing a Federal Register notice to implement a new immigration parole fee required by the H.R. 1 Reconciliation Bill.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Assisted in ICE Investigation Leading to Arrest of 370 Alien Offenders in Massachusetts
item.description: BOSTON – U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services provided valuable assistance to the investigation that led to the apprehension of 370 illegal aliens in Massachusetts between March 18 and 23.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Policy to Recognize Two Biological Sexes
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services is updating the USCIS Policy Manual to clarify that it only recognizes two biological sexes, male and female.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Tools Outage
item.description: USCIS will conduct system maintenance to the Contact Relationship Interface System (CRIS) on Wednesday, Feb. 19, 2025 at 11:50 p.m. through Thursday, Feb. 20, 2025 at 2:00 a.m. Eastern.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Filing Procedures for Form I-140
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services today announced a Federal Register notice (FRN) providing updated procedures for submitting a Form I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Workers, accompanied by a permanent labor certification, application for Schedule A designation, or national interest waiver (NIW) request.
item.dc:creator: USCIS
